Flag PCR errors using vsearch

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
flag_pcr_error.Rd

Identify potential PCR errors: ASVs that are highly similar (within max_mismatch) to a more abundant ASV, based on abundance ratios in the input dataset.

Usage

flag_pcr_error(
  unique_asv_df,
  vsearch_path = NULL,
  num_threads = 0,
  pcr_error_var_prop = 0.1,
  max_mismatch = 1,
  quiet = TRUE
)

Arguments

unique_asv_df

Data frame with the following columns: asv, read_count. ASVs must be unique.

vsearch_path

Optional path to the vsearch executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.vsearch_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

num_threads

Positive integer specifying the number of CPU threads to use. If 0, all available CPUs are used.

pcr_error_var_prop

Numeric value between 0 and 1 specifying the maximum allowed abundance ratio between similar ASVs. Less abundant ASVs below this threshold are flagged as PCR errors.

max_mismatch

Positive integer specifying the maximum number of mismatches (including gaps) used to define similarity between ASVs.

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppress informational messages and only display warnings or errors.

Value

Input data frame with an added PCRerror column (1 = potential PCR error, 0 = otherwise).

Details

A sequence is flagged as a potential PCR error when it is closely related to a more abundant ASV and its relative abundance is below pcr_error_var_prop. A new column is added to the input data frame: PCRerror (1 = potential PCR error, 0 = otherwise).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
unique_asv_df <- read_count_df %>%
  dplyr::group_by(asv) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(read_count = sum(read_count))

unique_asv_df_flagged <- flag_pcr_error(
  unique_asv_df,
  pcr_error_var_prop = 0.2,
  max_mismatch = 2
)
} # }
